JIMMY & WAX — PRODUCTION IMPLEMENTATION HANDOFF
Date: 2026-10-25

Outcome
-------
The implementation work identified by CROSS_PROJECT_AUDIT_2026-10-25.txt is complete locally across the dashboard, backend, website and Flutter app. The projects share OpenAPI contract 1.6.0, SHA-256 54c94cbcb6db670d06b11bb0fc59a94e6bd8a41d083ea3b86b6525337ed3c8a9. The release contract check verifies all five copies (backend canonical, backend pack, dashboard, website and app).

What changed
------------
* Catalog is variant-safe end to end: primary in-stock variant selection, variant media/price/stock, variant-specific web and app carts, category/collection routing and bounded cursor pagination.
* Customer workflows now cover account/profile/contact preferences, address book, wishlist, inbox, data export, account deletion with password or fresh bound-phone OTP, recovery and email verification, published policies, immutable invoices/orders, tracking, cancellation, return requests and verified-purchase reviews.
* The dashboard now has an explicit physical-return receipt action. It requires confirmation, restocks once, communicates the difference between queued prepaid refunds and manual COD reconciliation, and does not automatically replay a failed write.
* SMS, mail, storage, payment and shipping configuration are service-role-aware. Real provider secrets are never delivered to the public experience API.
* Shiprocket is prepared but intentionally OFF. The adapter supports API-user login or bearer token, safe refresh, read-only readiness, forward-shipment safety and the documented reverse-return payload. Approval never auto-books a reverse pickup; manual coordination remains the fallback until a controlled provider acceptance passes.
* Dependencies were updated and production dependency audits are clean. Production config rejects unsafe local/place-holder origins. `.env`, signing material, Flutter memory dumps and generated app artifacts are excluded from source control.
* Flutter is restored and has a reusable Windows build wrapper that handles the `&` in the original project path without changing the source folder.

Verification performed
----------------------
* Dashboard: contract, TypeScript, ESLint, 399 tests in 69 files, and Next production build passed.
* Backend: all 11 workspace TypeScript projects, formatting, 79 unit tests and 209 isolated PostgreSQL integration tests passed. A deliberately introduced type error made the type gate fail, then was removed.
* Website: contract, release-origin preflight, 70 unit tests, Vite production build, and 8 Chromium browser tests passed.
* App: `flutter analyze` passed; 236 tests passed with one intentional skip; a debug Android APK was built successfully using the normal wrapper command.
* Production-only package audits for dashboard, backend and website report zero vulnerabilities.
* A separate PostgreSQL backup/restore drill passed all 13 invariant checks. Local browser smoke coverage also exercised login, guest-cart merge, COD order, profile/preferences, policies, invoice, delivery tracking, return selection and review moderation against the isolated backend.

Raw logs and machine-readable audit outputs are in:
docs/build/evidence/production-readiness-2026-10-25

Owner activation gates (not code defects)
-----------------------------------------
1. Deploy the four projects to their real HTTPS origins and configure secrets in the hosting provider. Run the backend production preflight against managed Postgres, object storage and SMTP.
2. Confirm legal policy/GST/support/return-window content, DNS, monitoring, managed backup/PITR and source-repository remote baselines.
3. Run controlled real-provider acceptance for Razorpay, Twilio and Shiprocket. Shiprocket details are in the backend `docs/build/SHIPROCKET_ACTIVATION.txt`; credentials were deliberately not requested or stored here.
4. Provide Android release signing/Play access, iOS signing/team/Mac, and run physical-device release acceptance.

Explicitly deferred product decisions
-------------------------------------
Push/marketing automation and automatic reverse-pickup booking were not activated because they need separate consent, provider credentials and operational policy. The current return flow is safe: a customer request is approved, staff physically receive/restock it once, finance queues eligible prepaid refunds, and COD refunds remain manual and auditable.
